comments.author: frank
comments.body: Why not keep Decimal and just fix the serialisation? Decimal is the textbook answer for money. Integer cents gets awkward the moment you have fractional fees or FX.

comments.author: bob
comments.body: The textbook answer assumes one system. We talk to Stripe and two banks, and they are all integer minor units. Every Decimal<->int conversion at the edge was a chance to round differently, and that's where the JPY/KWD mismatches came from. Fractional fees are basis points on an int with explicit half-even rounding (`apply_bps`), so the rounding happens in exactly one place. FX will do the same.

comments.author: alice
comments.body: We discussed this at length at the sync. Going with integer minor units; it's in the ADR.

threads.rejection_reason: Superseded by ADR-007: money is int minor units, fee maths via apply_bps with explicit rounding.

comments.author: alice
comments.body: Can we make `apply_bps` the only way to do percentage maths on money? I'd rather people didn't write `amount * 29 // 1000` inline and pick their own rounding.

comments.author: bob
comments.body: Yes. Added a docstring and called it out in the ADR. Reviewers should push back on inline percentage maths.
